_about: Field terms for F81, same shape as papers/glossary.json.

reflectance-spectrum.definition: the share of light a surface reflects at each wavelength, here measured from 300 to 700 nm, which includes the ultraviolet below 400 nm
reflectance-spectrum.excludes: the colour a viewer sees, which also depends on the light and the eye

photoreceptor-class.definition: one kind of light-sensitive cell in the eye, defined by the wavelengths it responds to; humans have three cone classes, bees three including one for ultraviolet, blue tits four
photoreceptor-class.excludes: the rods used in dim light, and the nerve cells that compare receptor signals

quantum-catch.definition: the number of photons a receptor class absorbs from a surface, the sum over wavelength of reflectance times light times the receptor's sensitivity, here divided by the catch from a perfect white under the same light

von-kries.definition: scaling each receptor class's catch by its catch from a white under the same light, a simple model of how eyes adjust to the colour of the light
von-kries.excludes: adaptation that mixes signals between receptor classes

rnl.definition: the model of Vorobyev and Osorio in which two colours can be told apart when the difference in log receptor signals is large compared with the noise in each receptor class; brightness differences are left out
rnl.excludes: models of colour appearance, and any effect of pattern, motion or learning

jnd.definition: the unit of colour distance in the receptor-noise-limited model; a distance of 1 is treated as the threshold, so pairs at or below 1 count as indistinguishable for that observer
jnd.excludes: a measured threshold for a real animal on a real task

weber-fraction.definition: the noise in one receptor class as a fixed share of its signal, the same at every light level; we call a model with only this noise the Weber model
weber-fraction.excludes: photon noise, which grows in relative size as the catch falls

photon-noise.definition: the random variation in how many photons a receptor absorbs, which every real receptor has and which matters most when the catch is small; added here as a term that falls with the catch
photon-noise.excludes: noise in the nerve cells after the receptors

human-blind-pair.field: our usage, after the metamer of colour science
human-blind-pair.definition: a pair of surfaces whose modelled colour distance for the human trichromat is at most 1 JND, so the model says a person cannot tell them apart by colour; dog-blind pairs are defined the same way
human-blind-pair.excludes: pairs a person cannot tell apart by brightness, which the model does not test

separation-ratio.definition: among pairs one observer cannot separate, the share of flower-background pairs a second observer separates divided by the share of background-background pairs it separates; 1 means flowers gain nothing over the background
separation-ratio.excludes: how far apart the pairs are for the second observer

label-shuffle.definition: a control that randomly reassigns the flower and background labels over the same surfaces, here 500 times, and recomputes the separation ratio, which shows how large it gets when the labels carry no meaning
label-shuffle.excludes: a shuffle of the spectra themselves

uv-share.definition: a surface's mean reflectance below 400 nm divided by its mean reflectance from 400 to 700 nm
uv-share.excludes: whether the ultraviolet forms a pattern on the petal

pollination-syndrome.definition: the dataset's labels for flowers whose recorded pollinators are insects only or birds only
pollination-syndrome.excludes: flowers visited by both, which the dataset does not include in these groups

benjamini-hochberg.definition: a rule that adjusts a set of p values so that, among the tests called significant, the expected share of false calls stays at or below a chosen rate q, here 0.05
benjamini-hochberg.excludes: the stricter Bonferroni rule, which bounds the chance of any false call

instrument-check.field: our usage; a known-answer test of the model against behaviour
instrument-check.definition: a preregistered test in which the model must reproduce published behavioural measurements, here the smallest wavelength step each observer can detect; if it fails, only ranks and ratios from the model are used
instrument-check.excludes: a test of the model against its own output, and a planted check on synthetic data
